generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: flowers small, regular; calyx-lobes, petals and stamens 5 (or 4); petals hooded, sometimes wanting; calyx-tube lined with a disk on whose edge the petals and stamens are inserted; ovary free from or adnate by the disk to the base of the calyx, 3 (or 2)-celled. For cascara, Jepson eFlora calls the ovary more or less inferior while the Burke Herbarium and Jepson (1925) call it superior, free of the disk (as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read); the superior reading is kept.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 201 Rhamnaceae: trees or shrubs, very rarely herbs, sometimes climbing; leaves simple, alternate or opposite; stipules mostly present; fruit of several kinds, often a drupe.
